Ivern.escape: Right after Ivern Q Rootcaller is down, you have a chance to close the gap. Don’t engage first against Ivern’s ally affected by Ivern E Triggerseed; wait for the shield to burst. Use that opening to close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Ivern.build: If the enemy team is mostly ranged and keeps its distance, consider Rylai’s Crystal Scepter first. Ivern’s own damage is low, and it’s more dangerous when his allies follow up on his root and knockup, so consider Tenacity before building magic resistance just for Ivern.
Ivern.combo: Once Ivern Q Rootcaller is down and the shield from Ivern E Triggerseed has burst, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed. Then land the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. For Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit him with a skill to apply Dream Dust, then use it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Ivern.fight: After dodging Ivern Q Rootcaller, keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed and deal damage. Lillia’s main magic damage is effective against Ivern, who has low magic resistance. If Ivern E Triggerseed is on a target, don’t immediately go in with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!; engage after the shield bursts.
Ivern.laning: Early on, focus on clearing camps in succession and scaling rather than forcing kills. Ivern plants seeds in camps and returns to harvest them, so use early jungle vision to read his path. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed. Once the enemy moves inside the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along a wall.
Ivern.phase: Early on, Lillia clears and scales well, but her solo ganks are weak, so clear camps quickly.
Ivern.teamfight: From the flank, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows instead of standing on the front line. When Ivern’s team engages, use the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between them and your damage dealers. Avoid angles that require throwing Lillia E Swirlseed at enemies behind Ivern R Daisy!. If you’ve applied Dream Dust to multiple enemies before the teamfight, use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight, then coordinate with your allies to focus and wake sleeping targets one at a time.
Ivern.watch: If you’re rooted by Ivern Q Rootcaller, Ivern’s allies can dash in, so stand behind minions or terrain before he casts it. If Ivern R Daisy! starts attacking you, move away to avoid being knocked up by repeated attacks.

Shyvana.phase: Shyvana is weak early without stacks, but Lillia’s solo ganking is weak too, so look for opportunities while quickly cycling through camps. However, the more permanent stacks Shyvana builds, the harder she is to fight, so it’s important to slow her growth from the start.
Shyvana.teamfight: Spread out so multiple allies aren’t caught in Shyvana R Dragon's Descent’s path or area spells. From the flank, Lillia should apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows, then hit the engaging Shyvana with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between her and allied carries. If you can apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies before a teamfight and cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, coordinate with your allies on the order to wake them.
Shyvana.build: Build magic resistance first for the magic damage from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis, Shyvana E Molten Burst, and Shyvana R Dragon's Descent. Also build armor for her basic attack damage, and avoid relying on a large amount of health alone because she deals percent max-health damage.
Shyvana.combo: Slow the target first with Lillia E Swirlseed, hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Before casting Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit with a spell to apply Dream Dust, and use it when your allies can wait through the time it takes for the sleep to take hold.
Shyvana.escape: Look for a chance to pressure Shyvana when Shyvana R Dragon's Descent is down or her Fury bar is empty. If she engages with Shyvana R Dragon's Descent, hit her with Lillia E Swirlseed after she lands, not during the dash, to control your distance. You can also counterattack when Shyvana returns to human form and her empowered spells wear off.
Shyvana.fight: Deal damage with the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows to keep movement speed stacks up, and fight while maintaining distance from Shyvana. If she engages with Shyvana R Dragon's Descent, slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed after she lands. Aim for the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! once the slow is applied.
Shyvana.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly and scale instead of forcing solo gank kills. Shyvana is weak before building stacks, so take camps and objectives first when you get the chance to delay her growth. Before ganking, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks, then roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall once the enemy moves toward the inside of the lane.
Shyvana.watch: Shyvana R Dragon's Descent is unstoppable during its dash, so don’t try to interrupt her engage; avoid the landing point. If she gets close, Shyvana Q Emberstrike’s empowered basic attack and the area damage from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis are dangerous, so keep your distance. Also watch out for the slow and percent max-health damage from Shyvana E Molten Burst.

Gragas.laning: Early on, scale by clearing camps in succession instead of forcing kills. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed. If the opponent steps into the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall. Don’t stay where Gragas Q Barrel Roll has been placed.
Gragas.build: Prioritize movement speed so you can escape the telegraphed barrel and charge ranges. Build magic resistance instead of armor to withstand Gragas’s damage. Gragas W Drunken Rage deals damage based on your max health, so avoid relying on a large health build alone.
Gragas.combo: Roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall to slow the target, then aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first apply Dream Dust by hitting the target with an ability, and check that an ally can wait for the sleep to take effect. Deal heavy damage after the damage reduction from Gragas W Drunken Rage ends.
Gragas.escape: Right after Gragas E Body Slam is down is your chance to close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. If Gragas E Body Slam hits you, get out of the barrel’s radius before trying to counterattack. Chase a fleeing Gragas only when you can secure the kill.
Gragas.fight: Don’t try to deal heavy damage while Gragas drinks with W Drunken Rage; attack after its effect ends. Right after Gragas uses E Body Slam, close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, but avoid chasing deep. Keep hitting Gragas with Lillia Q Blooming Blows during the fight to maintain movement speed.
Gragas.phase: Early on, watch out for Gragas’s burst and focus on Lillia’s fast camp clear. In the mid game, use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby and coordinate with allies to create ganks and fights. If you withstand Gragas’s disruption in the early and mid game, the matchup improves as the game goes on and Lillia’s damage over time and movement speed come into their own.
Gragas.teamfight: Instead of standing in front, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows from the flank, and hit an engaging Gragas with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between him and your allied damage dealers. If possible, apply Dream Dust before the team fight and cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight. Coordinate target order with your allies and focus sleeping enemies one at a time.
Gragas.watch: When you see Gragas Q Barrel Roll, leave its radius immediately. If Gragas E Body Slam hits you near the barrel, you’re likely to be knocked up and then hit by the explosion, so build movement speed with Lillia Q Blooming Blows and keep your distance. When Gragas R Explosive Cask is available, don’t stand with your back to the enemy team.

Kayn.teamfight: Lillia shouldn’t stand on the frontline. From the side, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust. If Kayn dives in, use the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance between him and your carries, and prepare crowd control for when he emerges from Kayn R Umbral Trespass. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby puts multiple enemies to sleep, coordinate with your allies on whom to wake first and focus them one at a time.
Kayn.laning: Early on, focus on clearing camps quickly and scaling instead of forcing kills. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. Once an opponent steps toward the inside of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall. Pressure camps and objectives during Kayn’s weak pre-transformation phase, but don’t give up kills.
Kayn.build: Kayn’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so start with Cloth Armor and then get Plated Steelcaps. If the enemy team has an assassin, get Zhonya's Hourglass earlier. If Kayn transforms into Rhaast and you expect a long duel, build armor first, then consider Grievous Wounds.
Kayn.combo: Slow the target first with Lillia E Swirlseed, then aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit an ability first to apply Dream Dust, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect. If Kayn uses Kayn R Umbral Trespass to enter an ally, prepare crowd control for where he will emerge.
Kayn.escape: Don’t rush in when only Kayn Q Reaping Slash is down; Kayn can still escape with Kayn R Umbral Trespass. Look for an opening before Kayn R Umbral Trespass is back up, especially after dodging the line of Kayn W Blade's Reach, then close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Kayn.fight: Keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to maintain your movement speed stacks, and deal damage from the side. Dodge the line of Kayn W Blade's Reach, and look for an opening before Kayn R Umbral Trespass is back up. If Kayn enters a wall with Kayn E Shadow Step, damage him with Lillia Q Blooming Blows or Lillia E Swirlseed to shorten its duration.
Kayn.phase: Early on, pressure Kayn with camp and objective control: Lillia clears the jungle and scales well, while Kayn is weak before transforming. Lillia is strongest in the mid to late game, when her damage over time and movement speed improve, so prepare to fight during that stretch.
Kayn.watch: Dodge the line of Kayn W Blade's Reach. If it hits, it can set up Kayn R Umbral Trespass, so create distance when Kayn approaches from a wall or casts W. If a warning marker appears along a wall, stop fighting and fall back toward your turret.

MasterYi.teamfight: From the side, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust. If Master Yi R Highlander is inactive, hit Master Yi as he dives in with Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance between him and your carries. Don’t leave an ally alone for Master Yi to kill, since a takedown lets him immediately stick to his next target. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby puts enemies to sleep, coordinate with your allies on the target and focus them one at a time.
MasterYi.combo: When Master Yi R Highlander is down, slow him first with Lillia E Swirlseed, then hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Don’t rush your attack while Master Yi Q Alpha Strike is active; follow up after he lands. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit an ability first to apply Dream Dust, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
MasterYi.build: Early on, start with Cloth Armor to withstand physical damage and get Plated Steelcaps for boots. Armor doesn’t help against the true damage from Master Yi E Wuju Style, so also consider your total health and ways to create distance.
MasterYi.escape: Look for an opening right after Master Yi’s mobility tool, Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, is down. Confirm his landing, then close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. If Master Yi R Highlander is active, Lillia E Swirlseed’s slow won’t work, so engage carefully.
MasterYi.fight: Keep hitting Lillia Q Blooming Blows to maintain your movement speed stacks, and trade with the true damage at its edge. After making Master Yi use Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, you can look for a chance to close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! once he lands. Don’t rely on slows to fight while Master Yi R Highlander is active.
MasterYi.laning: Early on, focus on clearing camps quickly and scaling instead of forcing solo ganks. Sweep the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows across a group of monsters, and hit the large monster with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks.
MasterYi.phase: Early on, Lillia clears the jungle and scales well but has weak solo ganks, while Master Yi is weak in the jungle and at ganking. Clear camps quickly and disrupt Master Yi’s scaling with early objectives.
MasterYi.watch: Master Yi can’t be targeted while casting Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, so aim for him right after he lands. When Master Yi R Highlander is active, slows don’t work, so you can’t create distance with Lillia E Swirlseed. Master Yi’s basic attacks deal some true damage while Master Yi E Wuju Style is active, so don’t stay close and rely on armor alone.

Nunu.teamfight: From the side, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust, and hit Nunu & Willump as he dives in with Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance between him and your carries. When Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero begins, move out of range instead of forcing attacks. If you start a teamfight with Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, coordinate with your allies on whom to focus first so the sleeping targets don’t all wake at once.
Nunu.build: Get Morellonomicon early to counter the healing from Nunu & Willump Q Consume. For defenses, build magic resistance first to counter Nunu & Willump’s main damage, and consider tenacity to deal with crowd control.
Nunu.combo: After dodging Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and going in, slow him first with Lillia E Swirlseed. Then hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit an ability first to apply Dream Dust, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Nunu.escape: After dodging Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and avoiding the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, look for an opening to engage. Nunu & Willump has no ability to create distance, so slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, then close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Nunu.fight: After dodging Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed while fighting. Apply Grievous Wounds to counter healing from Nunu & Willump Q Consume, and close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! while the gap is not widening.
Nunu.laning: Instead of forcing solo ganks, clear camps quickly. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed.
Nunu.phase: In the mid to late game, make use of Lillia’s strengths as her damage over time and movement speed improve.
Nunu.watch: Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! travels a long distance and knocks you up. If you see it, don’t just run straight back; move toward the snowball and escape through the area Nunu passed. If Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage hits you, leave immediately before you’re rooted afterward. When Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero begins, get out of range before the slow becomes severe.

Rengar.watch: Rengar P Unseen Predator lets him leap from brush and build Ferocity, so avoid paths beside brush and secure vision when Rengar is unseen. Rengar E Bola Strike can root you when his Ferocity is full, so let it pass before using Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. When Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt is active, don’t roam alone while injured; stay with your allies.
Rengar.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly instead of trying to get kills through solo ganks. Just before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed. If the enemy moves toward the inside of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall. Avoid paths beside brush when Rengar is unseen.
Rengar.teamfight: Lillia should stay off the front line and hit multiple enemies from the flank with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Lillia P Dream-Laden Bough’s damage over time. If Rengar engages on an ally, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance, then catch him and focus him after Rengar W Battle Roar is down. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby puts multiple enemies to sleep, coordinate with your allies to wake and deal with them one at a time.
Rengar.build: Rengar’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so build armor first. Buy Cloth Armor early, choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots, and rush Zhonya's Hourglass in case the assassin Rengar catches you.
Rengar.combo: After confirming Rengar W Battle Roar is down, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit with a spell to set up the sleep, and cast it when your allies can wait for him to fall asleep.
Rengar.escape: Let Rengar E Bola Strike pass, then engage as soon as Rengar W Battle Roar is down. Rengar has no spell to create distance on his own, so close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and follow up with the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed.
Rengar.fight: Trade after Rengar’s Ferocity bar is empty and Rengar W Battle Roar is down. Keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed and aim for the true damage at its edge. If Rengar engages, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, create distance, then counterattack.
Rengar.phase: Early on, Lillia clears the jungle and scales well, but her solo ganking is weak, so keep clearing camps. Lillia is strongest in the mid and late game, when her damage over time and movement speed improve.

Vi.teamfight: Don’t stand on the frontline; approach from the flank and apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. When Vi engages, slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between her and your allied damage dealers, and don’t stay in front for long just to aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies before the team fight and cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby. Coordinate with your allies on the target order and focus on waking sleeping enemies one at a time.
Vi.build: Use Cloth Armor to survive the early game, and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Vi’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so build armor first. If the enemy team has an assassin, get Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier so you have a way to survive being caught once.
Vi.combo: Dodge Vi Q Vault Breaker or bait it out, then hit her with Lillia E Swirlseed to slow her. While she is slowed, hit her with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first apply Dream Dust with a spell, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Vi.escape: Vi Q Vault Breaker is her way to move, so right after you make her use it is your chance to engage. Close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! then, but don’t use displacement while Vi R Cease and Desist is charging toward you; wait until she lands and her knock-up ends.
Vi.fight: Vi W Denting Blows is strongest with repeated hits, so deal damage briefly and create distance. Keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed, and close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! right after dodging Vi Q Vault Breaker. If Vi P Blast Shield is active, wait for it to be removed before trading damage.
Vi.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly to scale instead of forcing kills. While clearing the jungle, hit the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows across a group of monsters and hit the large monster with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed. If the enemy moves toward the inner part of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
Vi.phase: Lillia clears and scales well early, but has weak solo ganks, so keep clearing camps. Lillia is at her strongest in the mid to late game, when items improve her damage over time and movement speed.
Vi.watch: Vi Q Vault Breaker deals heavy damage when fully charged, so move back or sidestep when you see her charging. Vi W Denting Blows reduces a target’s armor and increases Vi’s attack speed with repeated hits, so don’t stay in a long fight with her. Vi R Cease and Desist chases its target all the way, so you can’t dodge it with Flash; don’t try to stop her with displacement while she is charging in.

Briar.teamfight: Stay off the front line and apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows from the flank. If Briar engages on your allied damage dealers, slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed and position your front line in the path of Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby puts multiple enemies to sleep, coordinate with allies to focus and wake them one at a time.
Briar.laning: Early on, scale by clearing camps in succession instead of forcing kills. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to fill the movement speed stacks. If the opponent steps farther into the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall. Check entrances without vision with Lillia E Swirlseed.
Briar.build: Briar’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so use Cloth Armor early and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. If Briar’s healing becomes a problem in extended fights, consider Grievous Wounds after building armor.
Briar.combo: For a gank, bounce Lillia E Swirlseed off a wall or roll it and hit the target. While they’re slowed, hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first apply Dream Dust with an ability, and cast it when an ally can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Briar.escape: Don’t engage just because Briar Q Head Rush is down; check whether Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack and Briar R Certain Death are still available. In particular, close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! during the window when Briar’s mobility and crowd control are down, before Briar R Certain Death comes back up.
Briar.fight: Keep hitting Briar with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to maintain movement speed stacks, and trade while managing your distance with its true damage on the edge. When Briar dashes in, use the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance. While Briar still has her mobility ability, don’t force an attempt to hit the center of the telegraphed Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Briar.phase: Briar gets involved in kills often and engages frequently in the early game, so Lillia should clear camps quickly instead of forcing fights. Lillia is strongest in the mid and late game, when her damage over time and movement speed are bolstered.
Briar.watch: Briar Q Head Rush dashes in, stuns, and reduces armor, so watch her approach and dodge by creating distance. When Briar E Chilling Scream starts charging, move away from positions with a wall behind you. If Briar R Certain Death marks you as prey, move toward your allies and fight together instead of fleeing alone.

Graves.watch: Graves Q End of the Line detonates immediately when it hits a wall, so don’t fight with your back to a wall or in a narrow jungle passage. If you’re caught in Graves W Smoke Screen, your vision is blocked and you’re slowed, so leave its area by the shortest route. Graves P New Destiny’s basic attacks are blocked by the first unit hit, so keep minions or allies between you and him.
Graves.build: Graves deals mostly physical damage, and Lillia has low armor, so build armor first. Use Cloth Armor to survive the early game and buy Plated Steelcaps early.
Graves.combo: After confirming Graves’ mobility spell, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, land the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. For Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit him with a spell to set up the condition, then use it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Graves.escape: Don’t engage just because Graves E Quickdraw is down. Close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! before Graves R Collateral Damage comes back, especially while his other mobility option is also down. If Graves W Smoke Screen is active, leave its area first, then re-engage.
Graves.fight: Fight in open terrain with minions or an ally between you and Graves. While Graves reloads after firing two shots, land Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed, then retaliate or create distance. If Graves has stacked armor with E Quickdraw, aim to hit him with the true damage at the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows.
Graves.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly in succession instead of forcing solo ganks. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed. When the enemy moves inside the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along a wall. Take opportunities to pressure Graves before he can stack E Quickdraw.
Graves.phase: Lillia is strong in the mid to late game as her sustained damage and movement speed improve, but Graves also gets stronger as he stacks E Quickdraw, making him harder to deal with over time. Pressure him whenever possible from the early game to limit his chances to stack.
Graves.teamfight: From the flank, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows instead of trying to land the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! from the front, and slow enemies who engage with Lillia E Swirlseed. Before a teamfight starts, hit multiple enemies with your skills, then use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight. Coordinate with your allies on the order and wake and take down sleeping enemies one at a time.

Khazix.watch: Kha'Zix Q Taste Their Fear is a major threat to isolated targets, so stay near allies or minions. If Kha'Zix disappears with R Void Assault, don’t chase his position; roll Lillia E Swirlseed along his likely approach path. Secure vision in brushes to reduce the threat of the empowered basic attack and slow from Kha'Zix P Unseen Threat.
Khazix.fight: Fight near allies so you aren’t isolated, and keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed. Right after Kha'Zix E Leap is used to engage, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed and retaliate. Aim for the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! after he’s slowed.
Khazix.build: Buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Kha'Zix’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so build armor first. Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early as well so you can survive being caught once.
Khazix.combo: If Kha'Zix E Leap is down, slow him first with Lillia E Swirlseed, land the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby on targets you’ve first hit with a skill to apply Dream Dust, when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Khazix.escape: Right after Kha'Zix E Leap is used to engage, you have an opening to retaliate or close the gap. Slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, then close in with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. If Kha'Zix disappears with R Void Assault, stay near your allies and respond as soon as he reappears.
Khazix.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly in succession instead of looking for kills with solo ganks. Hit groups of monsters with the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows and large monsters with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed. When the enemy moves inside the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along a wall.
Khazix.phase: Early on, Lillia should focus on clearing and scaling. Before Kha'Zix’s first evolution, respond by pressuring the enemy jungle or securing objectives first. From midgame onward, once he has two or more evolutions, stop acting alone. In the mid to late game, when Lillia’s sustained damage and movement speed are improved, fight alongside your allies.
Khazix.teamfight: Group with allies in a narrow area where you have vision to avoid Kha'Zix Q Taste Their Fear’s isolated damage. From the flank, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust, and if Kha'Zix engages, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between him and your damage dealers. If you’ve applied Dream Dust to multiple enemies before the teamfight, use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight, then coordinate with your allies on the targets and wake sleeping enemies one at a time.

MonkeyKing.combo: After identifying Wukong’s clone so you don’t mistake it for the real champion, slow the real Wukong with Lillia E Swirlseed. While he’s slowed, hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit an ability first to apply Dream Dust, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
MonkeyKing.teamfight: If Wukong R Cyclone is up, don’t group with your allies. From the side, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. If Wukong dives in, use the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance between him and your carries. To start a teamfight, apply Dream Dust in advance, then cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of vision. Coordinate with your allies on the order of sleeping targets and wake them one at a time.
MonkeyKing.build: Early on, start with Cloth Armor to survive and get Plated Steelcaps for boots. Wukong’s damage is mainly physical, and Lillia has low armor, so build armor first. However, Wukong Q Crushing Blow reduces armor, and Wukong E Nimbus Strike deals magic damage, so don’t rely on armor alone in a long fight.
MonkeyKing.escape: Both Wukong W Warrior Trickster and Wukong E Nimbus Strike are mobility tools, so don’t engage just because one is down. In particular, look for an opening before Wukong W Warrior Trickster is back up, then close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. You can also look to force a fight or objective right after Wukong R Cyclone is down.
MonkeyKing.fight: Lillia’s magic damage works well against Wukong’s low magic resistance, but the longer Wukong stays in a fight, the more armor and healing he builds up. Hit him with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed, then repeat short trades where you deal damage and back off. Avoid a long duel where Wukong catches you with Wukong E Nimbus Strike and follows up with Wukong Q Crushing Blow.
MonkeyKing.laning: Early on, clear camps in succession and scale instead of hunting for kills with solo ganks. Sweep the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows across a group of monsters, and hit the large monster with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Before ganking, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed. Once an opponent steps toward the inside of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
MonkeyKing.phase: Early on, Lillia clears camps and scales well but has weak solo ganks, so clear camps quickly. In the mid to late game, when her damage over time and movement speed improve, Lillia is at her strongest, so take advantage of opportunities to fight.
MonkeyKing.watch: Wukong E Nimbus Strike is a targeted dash, so avoid it from outside its range. When Wukong W Warrior Trickster creates a clone, don’t waste abilities on the clone left behind; watch where the real Wukong will move.

Poppy.teamfight: From the side, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust, and hit Poppy as she dives in with Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance between her and your carries. If you applied Dream Dust to multiple enemies before the teamfight, cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of vision. Coordinate with your allies on which sleeping enemy to wake first, and don’t force the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! from the front.
Poppy.build: Poppy’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so start with Cloth Armor to survive. Get Plated Steelcaps for boots to build armor. Poppy Q Hammer Shock deals damage based on your max health, so don’t rely on stacking health alone.
Poppy.combo: After Poppy E Heroic Charge is down and Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends, slow her first with Lillia E Swirlseed. Then hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Apply Dream Dust with an ability before using Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Poppy.escape: Look for a chance to close the gap right after Poppy uses Poppy E Heroic Charge. If Poppy W Steadfast Presence is also active, wait for it to end, then go in with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Poppy.fight: Make Poppy use Poppy E Heroic Charge, then fight in an open area while managing your distance. Hit with the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows to use its true damage and build movement speed stacks. Don’t dive in with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! while Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active.
Poppy.laning: Early on, clear camps in succession instead of forcing solo kills. Sweep the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows across a group of monsters, and hit the large monster with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. Once an opponent steps toward the inside of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
Poppy.phase: Early on, Lillia clears camps and scales well but has weak solo ganks, so clear camps quickly. In the mid to late game, make use of Lillia’s strengths as her damage over time and movement speed improve.
Poppy.watch: Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns you if you hit a wall, so stand in an open area with no wall behind you. If Poppy Q Hammer Shock hits you, immediately walk out of the zone where the second hit will land. If Poppy starts charging Poppy R Keeper's Verdict, move sideways out of its path.

Shaco.escape: The moment Shaco appears after entering a fight with Shaco Q Deceive is your chance to catch him. Close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and attack with your allies. If you expect Shaco W Jack In The Box in an area, check vision first so you don’t engage while feared.
Shaco.teamfight: From the flank, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. If Shaco approaches your allied carries, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance. When Shaco appears after entering with Shaco Q Deceive, focus the real Shaco with your allies. Watch the health bar’s reaction so you don’t waste damage on the Shaco R Hallucinate clone; when the clone dies, move away to avoid its explosion and fear.
Shaco.watch: If Shaco gets behind you with Shaco Q Deceive, his empowered basic attack is dangerous, so stand with your back to a wall or face your allies if you think Shaco is nearby. Watch for the fear from Shaco W Jack In The Box around brush you have no vision of and objectives; check first with Oracle Lens or a Control Ward. When low on health, don’t cross jungle areas where you have no vision and Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison could hit you.
Shaco.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand the damage from Shaco W Jack In The Box, Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison, and Shaco R Hallucinate. Since Shaco Q Deceive can let him catch you all at once, rush Zhonya's Hourglass too. Build health as well so you stay out of the health range where Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison deals increased damage.
Shaco.combo: Against Shaco, slow him first with Lillia E Swirlseed, hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit with a spell to apply Dream Dust, and use it when your allies can wait for the sleep.
Shaco.fight: Before a fight, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. Right after Shaco enters with Shaco Q Deceive, focus your damage on the real Shaco with your allies. Slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, then cast Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Aim for the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! when the target is slowed or asleep.
Shaco.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly and scale instead of solo ganking, and maintain vision at your jungle entrances to watch for Shaco invading. In camps, catch the monster group with the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows and hit the large monster with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. When ganking, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall after the enemy moves toward the inside of the lane.
Shaco.phase: Early on, watch for Shaco’s ganks and invades while Lillia clears camps quickly. If you avoid giving up early kills and buy time, Shaco’s solo fighting power falls off later.

Viego.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly instead of trying to get kills with solo ganks. Just before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed. If the enemy moves toward the inner part of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall. Don’t push the lane toward the direction where Viego E Harrowed Path is visible.
Viego.teamfight: From the flank, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows, and use Lillia E Swirlseed to slow an engaging Viego and create space between him and your allied damage dealers. If you applied Dream Dust before the fight, cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight, then coordinate with your allies to wake sleeping enemies one at a time, choosing a target together. Don’t continue fighting where an ally has fallen, and keep Viego from reaching that spot.
Viego.build: Use Cloth Armor to survive the early game, and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Viego’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so build armor first. If a duel drags on and the healing from Viego P Sovereign's Domination and Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King becomes a problem, consider Grievous Wounds after building resistances.
Viego.combo: First, bounce Lillia E Swirlseed off a wall or roll it to slow Viego. While he is slowed, hit him with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit him with a spell to apply Dream Dust, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Viego.escape: Even after Viego W Spectral Maw is down, don’t rush in to chase if Viego R Heartbreaker is still available. Look for an opening before Viego R Heartbreaker comes back, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, then close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Viego.fight: Keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed, and fight at its outer edge’s true damage range to maintain distance. After dodging Viego W Spectral Maw’s stun, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed and aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! while he is moving slowly. In skirmishes you cannot win, retreat without giving up a kill.
Viego.phase: Lillia clears and scales well early, but has weak solo ganks, so focus on clearing camps. Lillia is strongest in the mid to late game, when items improve her damage over time and movement speed. At every stage, it’s important not to give Viego a kill.
Viego.watch: Viego W Spectral Maw stuns for longer the more it is charged, so sidestep when you see him charging. If you see Viego E Harrowed Path on terrain, Viego may be camouflaged nearby, so avoid that area. When your health is low, fall back because you are an easy target for Viego R Heartbreaker.

Belveth.build: Use Cloth Armor to survive the early game, and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Bel'Veth Q Void Surge and Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom deal mostly physical damage, so build armor first. You can’t reduce the true damage from Bel'Veth R Endless Banquet with resistances.
Belveth.combo: First hit Bel'Veth with Lillia E Swirlseed to slow her, follow with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Engage in this sequence after dodging Bel'Veth W Above and Below and waiting for Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom to end. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit her with a spell to apply Dream Dust.
Belveth.escape: If Bel'Veth W Above and Below misses, she won’t get the cooldown reset for Bel'Veth Q Void Surge, so look for an opening to engage then. Even when Bel'Veth Q Void Surge is down, it can come back soon, so slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed and close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Also take advantage of the fact that Bel'Veth cannot immediately dash again in the direction she just dashed.
Belveth.fight: Keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed, and trade from a distance using its outer edge’s true damage. After sidestepping Bel'Veth W Above and Below, slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed and aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. If Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom is active, don’t deal heavy damage until it ends.
Belveth.laning: Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed. If the enemy moves toward the inner part of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall to try to slow them.
Belveth.phase: Bel'Veth is weak early, but Lillia also has weak solo ganks, so suppress Bel'Veth’s growth with fast camp clears and favorable early encounters. Bel'Veth’s growth stacks are permanent, making her harder to deal with as the game goes on, so it’s best to keep her down early.
Belveth.teamfight: From the flank, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows, and hit an engaging Bel'Veth with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between her and your allied damage dealers. If possible, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies before the fight, then cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight. Coordinate with your allies on the order and wake sleeping enemies one at a time. If an ally falls and Bel'Veth can get Void Coral, retreat; delay the team fight while Bel'Veth’s transformation is active.
Belveth.watch: Bel'Veth W Above and Below slows and knocks you up, and also resets the cooldown of Bel'Veth Q Void Surge. When Bel'Veth gets close, don’t run straight back; turn to the side to dodge W. Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom reduces the damage she takes while it is active, so save spells that deal heavy damage until it ends.

Amumu.teamfight: When Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is available, don’t group with allies; keep your distance in open terrain. From the flank, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows, then hit an Amumu who engages with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between him and your allied damage dealers. If you’ve applied Dream Dust to multiple enemies, use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby before the fight fully breaks out, then focus and wake sleeping enemies one at a time.
Amumu.build: Prioritize movement speed so you can escape Amumu’s telegraphed damage, and build magic resistance for defense. Amumu W Despair deals damage based on your max health, so avoid relying on a large health build alone.
Amumu.combo: Bounce Lillia E Swirlseed off a wall or roll it to slow Amumu first. While he’s slowed, hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first apply Dream Dust by hitting him with an ability.
Amumu.escape: Engage when Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy are down. Amumu has no ability to create distance on his own, so slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, then close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Amumu.fight: Keep hitting Amumu with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to maintain movement speed stacks and manage your distance. Once Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy are down, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed and aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Amumu.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly in succession instead of trying to get kills with solo ganks. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. If the opponent moves deeper into the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
Amumu.phase: In the mid and late game, Lillia’s damage over time and movement speed come into their own, so fight while avoiding Amumu’s stun.
Amumu.watch: If Amumu Q Bandage Toss hits you, you’ll be stunned and may then be caught by Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy if he gets close. Q Bandage Toss stops at the first target it hits, so keep a minion or jungle monster between you and Amumu. When R Curse of the Sad Mummy is available, spread out from allies and keep your distance.

Diana.teamfight: Spread out from allies so multiple teammates aren’t pulled in together by Diana R Moonfall, and use vision to watch for her flank angle. From the flank, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows, then hit a Diana who engages with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between her and your allied damage dealers. If you’ve applied Dream Dust to multiple enemies before the team fight starts, cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight.
Diana.combo: Hit the target with Lillia E Swirlseed to slow them first, then aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first apply Dream Dust with an ability, and check that an ally can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Diana.escape: If Diana uses E Lunar Rush to engage without marking you with Q Crescent Strike, slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed and take the chance to counterattack. If she engages while you’re marked, Diana E Lunar Rush resets, so create distance instead of trying to pin her down.
Diana.fight: Just before a fight, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. Sidestep Diana Q Crescent Strike, then fight from the flank while continuing to hit her with Lillia Q Blooming Blows after the orbs and shield from Diana W Pale Cascade are gone.
Diana.laning: Early on, scale by clearing camps quickly instead of forcing kills. Clip the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows through a group of monsters and hit the large monster with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. When ganking, wait for the opponent to move deeper into the lane, then roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
Diana.phase: Lillia is strongest in the mid and late game, when items bolster her damage over time and movement speed, so keep clearing camps instead of fixating on early kills.
Diana.watch: Diana Q Crescent Strike curves through the air and leaves a Moonlight mark, so when you see it, sidestep instead of only backing away. If you’re marked, Diana E Lunar Rush can dash in again; slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed and create distance. After Diana W Pale Cascade activates, don’t commit to close combat until its shield and orbs are gone.
Diana.build: If the enemy team has an assassin, build Zhonya's Hourglass earlier so Lillia has a way to survive if she gets caught while closing in and spinning Q. Build magic resistance over armor to prepare for Diana's damage.

Hecarim.teamfight: Spread out so Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows doesn’t fear multiple allies at once. From the flank, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust, and hit an engaging Hecarim with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between him and your damage dealers. If you start the teamfight with Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, coordinate with your allies on the targets and wake sleeping enemies one at a time.
Hecarim.build: Buy Cloth Armor first to survive the early game, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Hecarim’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so build armor first.
Hecarim.combo: Hit Hecarim with Lillia E Swirlseed first to slow him. While he’s slowed, land the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit him with a skill to apply Dream Dust, then cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Hecarim.escape: Don’t rush in when only Hecarim E Devastating Charge is down; he can escape with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. Look for an opening before Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows comes back, and close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Hecarim.fight: When Hecarim approaches, slow him first with Lillia E Swirlseed to reduce both his movement speed and damage. Keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed, and trade from a distance using its edge’s true damage.
Hecarim.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly instead of forcing kills. Hit groups of monsters with the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows and large monsters with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Q to stack movement speed. When the enemy moves inside the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along a wall.
Hecarim.phase: Both champions clear camps quickly early on, but Lillia has weak solo ganks, so focus on scaling.
Hecarim.watch: The farther Hecarim has run with E Devastating Charge, the more damage and knockback it deals. If he circles around and starts running from the other side, he may be building up distance, so move toward your allies and slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed. In teamfights, spread out because Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows can fear multiple targets.

Kindred.teamfight: Lillia shouldn’t stand on the frontline. From the side, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust. Apply Dream Dust before a teamfight, then cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of vision. Coordinate with your allies to focus sleeping targets one at a time. When Kindred R Lamb's Respite is active, have low-health allies stay inside its area to survive and receive the heal when it ends.
Kindred.build: Kindred’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so start with Cloth Armor and then get Plated Steelcaps. If duels still run long after you build resistances because of Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy and Kindred R Lamb's Respite, consider Grievous Wounds.
Kindred.combo: Slow the target first with Lillia E Swirlseed, then hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Kindred can escape with Kindred Q Dance of Arrows or Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy, so look for a chance to land Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! while those mobility abilities are down. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit an ability first to apply Dream Dust, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Kindred.escape: Don’t rush in when only Kindred Q Dance of Arrows is down; Kindred can still escape with Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy. Look for an opening before Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy is back up. If Kindred E Mounting Dread is applied, use the movement speed from Lillia Q Blooming Blows to create distance first.
Kindred.fight: Before a fight, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed, then keep hitting Q from the side while managing your distance. Look for an opening before Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy is back up. If Kindred Q Dance of Arrows is also down, slow them with Lillia E Swirlseed, then aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Kindred.laning: Early on, focus on clearing camps in succession and scaling instead of forcing solo kills. Clear camps marked by P Mark of the Kindred first, or secure vision nearby to delay Kindred from claiming the mark. When ganking, wait for the opponent to step toward the inside of the lane, then roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
Kindred.phase: Early on, Lillia clears camps quickly, but her solo ganks are weak, so focus on scaling and disrupting P Mark of the Kindred. In the mid to late game, when items improve her damage over time and movement speed, make use of Lillia’s strengths to keep fighting.
Kindred.watch: If Kindred E Mounting Dread is applied, use the movement speed from Lillia Q Blooming Blows to create distance and avoid taking follow-up hits. Its damage is more dangerous at low health, so don’t keep fighting when your health is especially low. Don’t stay long in the area of Kindred W Wolf's Frenzy, where Kindred Q Dance of Arrows comes back up more often.

RekSai.laning: Early on, keep clearing camps quickly instead of trying to get kills. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed. If the enemy moves toward the inside of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall. If you spot an entrance to Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel near a lane or in your own jungle, walk over it to destroy it.
RekSai.teamfight: Stay off the front line and hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows from the flank to apply damage over time. If Rek'Sai engages, use the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between her and your allied carries. Before a teamfight, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies and cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby. Coordinate with your team to focus and wake sleeping enemies one at a time.
RekSai.build: Buy Cloth Armor first to withstand Rek'Sai’s main physical damage early. Choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots and build armor first. Armor can’t reduce the true damage from Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel.
RekSai.combo: Hit with Lillia E Swirlseed first to slow the target, then aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Before casting Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit with a spell to apply Dream Dust, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep.
RekSai.escape: After dodging the knock-up from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, you have a chance to close the gap. Don’t go in just because Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel is down; look for a window before Rek'Sai R Void Rush comes back up. Use Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! to close the gap during that window.
RekSai.fight: Early on, don’t rush into solo fights; clear camps and scale. In fights, keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed, trade with the edge’s true damage, and maintain distance. If Rek'Sai Burrows to heal, keep Lillia P Dream-Laden Bough’s damage over time on her to offset the healing.
RekSai.phase: Early on, focus on farming without giving up kills, since Rek'Sai will try to build an advantage through ganks. Lillia becomes stronger in the mid and late game as her damage over time and movement speed improve.
RekSai.watch: When Rek'Sai goes underground with Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, watch for the knock-up and move toward open space, away from walls and narrow paths. Dodge the knock-up with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! as Rek'Sai emerges. If Rek'Sai has recently damaged you, Rek'Sai R Void Rush may be coming, so stay close to your allies.

Elise.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly instead of seeking kills with solo ganks, and secure vision so Elise’s early ganks don’t get kills. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed. If the opponent steps into the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
Elise.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand Elise’s main damage. Armor is also valuable because she deals damage with basic attacks, and if the enemy team has an assassin, get Zhonya’s Hourglass early.
Elise.combo: Slow Elise first with Lillia E Swirlseed, then hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. If Elise is airborne with E Rappel, roll Lillia E Swirlseed in advance to where she’ll land, then follow up after she comes down. Use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby after first applying Dream Dust with an ability, when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Elise.escape: Right after Elise uses Q Neurotoxin / Venomous Bite is your chance to close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. If both Elise E Cocoon and E Rappel are down, turn the tables and engage her.
Elise.fight: Keep hitting Elise with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed and deal damage from the flank while managing your distance. Don’t aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! from the front while Elise E Cocoon is available. Right after Elise Q Neurotoxin / Venomous Bite, you can close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Elise.phase: Elise is dangerous early as she looks to gain an advantage with ganks, so Lillia should clear camps without giving up kills.
Elise.teamfight: Instead of holding the front line, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows from the flank. If Elise engages, slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between her and your allied damage dealers. If you applied Dream Dust and used Lillia R Lilting Lullaby before the team fight, coordinate with your allies to focus each sleeping enemy one at a time.
Elise.watch: When Elise transforms with R Spider Form, she’s looking to finish off a low-health opponent, so be especially careful about when you use Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.

Jax.teamfight: From the flank, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows, and hit an engaging Jax with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between him and your damage dealers. If he comes in with Jax E Counter Strike active, don’t group nearby; avoid the area stun, then focus him with crowd control. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby puts multiple enemies to sleep, coordinate with your allies and wake and eliminate them one at a time.
Jax.build: Get an attack speed slow early to counter Jax’s basic attacks and attack speed. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so consider both armor and magic resistance.
Jax.combo: Slow him first with Lillia E Swirlseed, then aim for the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. If Jax E Counter Strike is active, move outside the stun area and wait for it to end before following this sequence. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit him with a skill to apply Dream Dust, and make sure your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Jax.escape: Right after you bait Jax Q Leap Strike, his mobility is down and you have an opening to engage. If Jax E Counter Strike has also ended, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, then go in with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Jax.fight: Look to trade after Jax E Counter Strike is down, and keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to maintain movement speed stacks. Right after Jax uses Q Leap Strike, you can close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, but wait until he’s slowed before aiming for the center hit.
Jax.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly and scale instead of forcing solo fights. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed. When the enemy moves inside the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along a wall.
Jax.phase: The mid to late game, when sustained damage and movement speed have improved, is when Lillia comes into her own.
Jax.watch: Jax E Counter Strike negates basic attacks and stuns in an area when reactivated. If Jax closes in with Q Leap Strike and activates E Counter Strike, stop basic attacking and move outside the stun area until its duration ends.

LeeSin.teamfight: From the side, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust, and hit Lee Sin as he dives in with Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance between him and your carries. If you applied Dream Dust before the teamfight, cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of vision. Keep your distance so you don’t collide with an ally hit by Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage. Coordinate with your allies on which sleeping enemy to wake first, then focus them one at a time.
LeeSin.build: Early on, start with Cloth Armor to survive and get Plated Steelcaps for boots. Lee Sin’s main damage is physical, and Lillia has low armor, so build armor first. If the enemy team has an assassin, get Zhonya's Hourglass earlier too.
LeeSin.combo: Slow the target first with Lillia E Swirlseed, then aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit an ability first to apply Dream Dust, and cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
LeeSin.escape: Both Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike and Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will are mobility tools, so don’t engage just because one is down. In particular, look for an opening before Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike is back up, then close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Focus your damage right after Lee Sin uses W to engage, while he has no shield or lifesteal.
LeeSin.fight: Don’t accept a straight duel with Lee Sin early on. Keep hitting Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks and manage your distance. If Lee Sin dives in, create distance with the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed. You can close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! before Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike is back up.
LeeSin.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly instead of hunting for kills with solo ganks. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. Once an opponent steps toward the inside of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
LeeSin.phase: Lee Sin is strong in early duels, so back off if you encounter him in the jungle and focus on Lillia’s fast camp clear. Lillia gets stronger in the mid to late game, when her damage over time and movement speed improve, so secure objectives and lane advantages to buy time until then.
LeeSin.watch: If health has dropped below half, stay near an allied turret or the team while a second hit is available. Stay away from walls where there is no vision on the other side, since Lee Sin can cross them with Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will.

Nocturne.laning: Keep clearing camps without interrupting your route to scale early. Just before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. If the enemy moves toward the inner part of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall to slow them, then engage.
Nocturne.teamfight: When Nocturne R Paranoia darkens your screen, don’t get isolated; immediately move toward your allies. From the flank, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows, and slow an engaging Nocturne with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between him and your allied damage dealers. When casting Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, coordinate with your allies to focus on waking sleeping targets one at a time.
Nocturne.watch: After Nocturne Q Duskbringer hits you, Nocturne can quickly approach along its trail, so don’t run in a straight line; turn toward an ally or turret. If Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror connects, you will be feared, so save Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! to create distance. Don’t use a key spell right away while Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is active.
Nocturne.build: Buy Cloth Armor first in the early game, and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Nocturne deals mostly physical damage, and Lillia has low armor, so prioritize armor. Get Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier as well so you can survive being caught once.
Nocturne.combo: If Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is active, first break the spell shield with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Then slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby after applying Dream Dust with a spell, when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Nocturne.escape: If Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror is still available, don’t use Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! carelessly; save it so you can create distance as soon as the tether connects.
Nocturne.fight: Early on, clear camps quickly instead of trying to get solo kills. While Nocturne R Paranoia is down, you have an opening to close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. During a fight, keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to maintain movement speed stacks, and create distance first if Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror connects.
Nocturne.phase: Lillia clears the jungle and scales well early, but has weak solo ganks, so prioritize camps. Lillia gets stronger in the mid to late game as items improve her damage over time and movement speed.

Fiddlesticks.combo: Land Lillia E Swirlseed first to slow them, then aim for the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby after applying Dream Dust with a spell, when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect. Keep in mind that sleep won’t apply immediately if Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest is channeling.
Fiddlesticks.teamfight: Secure vision in the brushes and approach paths near objectives, and spread out from allies so you aren’t all hit by Fiddlesticks’ area-of-effect skills. From the flank, hit multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to apply Dream Dust, then use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight. If Fiddlesticks engages, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between him and your damage dealers. Don’t keep fighting inside his ultimate’s area.
Fiddlesticks.build: Prioritize magic resistance against Fiddlesticks’ main damage. Use the movement speed stacks from Lillia Q Blooming Blows to escape the warned area of Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm. If the enemy team is mostly ranged and keeps its distance, build Rylai’s Crystal Scepter to stay on them longer after landing Q.
Fiddlesticks.escape: When Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm is down, that’s your chance to engage. Once you’ve confirmed Fiddlesticks Q Terrify and Fiddlesticks E Reap are down too, approach with less risk of being locked down by crowd control. Stack movement speed with Lillia Q Blooming Blows and close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!
Fiddlesticks.fight: Keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed, and deal sustained damage while adjusting your distance from the flank. Don’t stay in the area and allow Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest to heal him; leave its area. After Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm is down, look for a chance to close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!
Fiddlesticks.phase: Early on, Lillia should focus on fast jungle clears and scaling rather than solo ganks.
Fiddlesticks.watch: If Fiddlesticks disappears from sight for a long time, he may be preparing Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm in a brush, so check the brushes and approach paths near objectives. If you see him channeling, interrupt him with the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed; if you can’t interrupt him, leave the area. Skills that hit from out of sight can apply Terrify, so don’t walk past a stationary Scarecrow Effigy without checking around it.
Fiddlesticks.laning: Early on, focus on clearing camps back-to-back and scaling instead of forcing kills. Just before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build up movement speed. If the opponent moves deeper into lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall. Keep vision in the brush behind the lane to watch for Fiddlesticks's fear and ambushes from out of sight.

Evelynn.watch: When you see the mark from Evelynn W Allure, she’s nearby preparing to charm you, so retreat before the mark matures and alert your allies. At low health, watch out for the empowered damage from Evelynn R Last Caress and stay out of areas without vision.
Evelynn.teamfight: Stay off the front line and apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows from the flank. Roll Lillia E Swirlseed along Evelynn’s approach to your allied damage dealers to slow her and create distance. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby puts multiple enemies to sleep, coordinate with your allies to focus and wake them one at a time.
Evelynn.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand Evelynn Q Hate Spike, W Allure, and E Whiplash. Evelynn W Allure lowers magic resistance, so retreating before the mark matures is the priority. Get Zhonya’s Hourglass early as well so you can survive if Evelynn catches you.
Evelynn.combo: If the opponent moves deeper into the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall to slow them, hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first apply Dream Dust by hitting the target with an ability, and cast it when an ally can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Evelynn.escape: Don’t engage just because Evelynn E Whiplash is down. Look for a window before Evelynn R Last Caress comes back up, dodge Evelynn W Allure’s charm, then close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Evelynn.fight: Early on, scale by clearing camps quickly instead of forcing kills. Before Evelynn W Allure’s mark matures, slow her with Lillia E Swirlseed and manage your distance with the movement speed from hitting her with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. You can look to engage before Evelynn R Last Caress comes back up.
Evelynn.laning: While clearing camps, clip the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows through a group of monsters and hit the large monster with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Place vision beside Evelynn’s jungle camps to see where she starts fights.
Evelynn.phase: In the mid and late game, Lillia’s damage over time and movement speed are stronger, so build up damage on multiple enemies from the flank.

Karthus.teamfight: From the flank, apply sustained damage to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows and slow approaching enemies with Lillia E Swirlseed. Don’t stay in Karthus E Defile’s area for long. If you kill Karthus, stay away from his corpse until Karthus P Death Defied ends. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby puts multiple enemies to sleep, coordinate with your allies and focus them one at a time.
Karthus.build: Prioritize magic resistance over armor against Karthus’ damage. However, dodging Karthus W Wall of Pain and limiting your time in Karthus E Defile’s area come first. If the enemy team is mostly ranged and keeps its distance, build Rylai’s Crystal Scepter to stay on them longer after landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows.
Karthus.combo: Slow them first with Lillia E Swirlseed, land the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit them with a skill to apply Dream Dust, then use it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Karthus.escape: Slow them with Lillia E Swirlseed and close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. Don’t stand where Karthus Q Lay Waste is warned to land.
Karthus.fight: Approach while avoiding Karthus W Wall of Pain, and keep landing Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed and leave the warned areas of Karthus Q Lay Waste. Karthus has no skill to create distance himself, so when you have a chance to approach, close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. After killing him, move away from his corpse immediately because of Karthus P Death Defied.
Karthus.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly in succession instead of forcing solo kills. Hit groups of monsters with the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows and large monsters with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Karthus.phase: Lillia gets stronger in the mid to late game as items improve her sustained damage and movement speed, but you must keep enough health to survive Karthus R Requiem.
Karthus.watch: Karthus Q Lay Waste deals heavy damage when it hits you alone, so walk out of its warned area. Karthus W Wall of Pain slows and reduces magic resistance, so go around the wall. Even after Karthus is killed, he can cast skills near his corpse with Karthus P Death Defied, so move away immediately and keep enough health after a fight to survive Karthus R Requiem.

Taliyah.combo: Hit Taliyah with Lillia E Swirlseed from an angle where she hasn’t laid down a field of rocks to slow her. Then aim for the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Before using Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, hit with a spell to apply Dream Dust, and use it when your allies can wait for the sleep.
Taliyah.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand the magic damage from Taliyah Q Threaded Volley and Taliyah E Unraveled Earth. If the enemy composition is mostly ranged and keeps its distance, include Rylai's Crystal Scepter to extend the time you can stay on them with the slow from Lillia Q Blooming Blows.
Taliyah.escape: The chance to engage is after Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is down and before Taliyah R Weaver's Wall comes back up. If only one is down, account for the remaining mobility option before going in. Check that your angle avoids crossing the rock field before closing the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Taliyah.fight: Dodge Taliyah Q Threaded Volley sideways while continuing to land Lillia Q Blooming Blows to maintain movement speed stacks. Don’t cross Taliyah E Unraveled Earth with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!; go around it. When you have an opening to get close, use Lillia’s main source of magic damage to exploit Taliyah’s low magic resistance.
Taliyah.laning: Early on, keep clearing camps back to back and scale instead of forcing kills. Just before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. If Taliyah moves toward the inside of the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall. If Taliyah disappears from the jungle, watch for Taliyah P Rock Surfing, which speeds her up near walls, and for her to use Taliyah R Weaver's Wall to affect another lane.
Taliyah.phase: Early on, Lillia should focus on scaling and clearing camps, and attempt solo ganks carefully. Lillia gets stronger in the mid and late game as her damage over time and movement speed improve with items, so look for fights then.
Taliyah.teamfight: From the flank, apply damage over time to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows instead of aiming for the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! from the front. If an enemy engages, use the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed to create space between them and your allied carries. If you applied Dream Dust to multiple enemies before the teamfight, cast Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of vision, then coordinate with your allies to wake sleeping targets one at a time.
Taliyah.watch: Don't use Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! over the field of rocks. Taliyah Q Threaded Volley can't change direction while being cast, so sidestep it.

Brand.build: Build magic resistance before armor or health to withstand Brand’s damage. If the enemy team is mostly ranged and keeps its distance, buy Rylai’s Crystal Scepter to stay in range longer with Lillia Q Blooming Blows.
Brand.combo: Slow Brand first with Lillia E Swirlseed, then hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby after applying Dream Dust with an ability, when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
Brand.escape: The moment Brand W Pillar of Flame goes down is your chance to engage. If you’re ablaze, avoid the stun from Brand Q Sear; once the fire goes out, close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Brand.fight: Close the gap when Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and you aren’t ablaze. Keep hitting Brand with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed, and walk out of the spots where his attacks are telegraphed.
Brand.laning: Early on, focus on clearing camps quickly instead of forcing kills. Before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to stack movement speed. If Brand moves deeper into the lane, roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
Brand.phase: Early on, Lillia is better off focusing on scaling and clearing the jungle.
Brand.teamfight: Before engaging, spread out from allies to reduce the spread of Brand E Conflagration and the bounces of Brand R Pyroclasm. From the flank, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows, then use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby from out of sight before the team fight begins. Coordinate with your allies to focus and wake sleeping enemies one at a time.
Brand.watch: Dodge Brand W Pillar of Flame and Brand Q Sear first to prevent Blaze stacks and an explosion. If you’re ablaze, move out of Brand Q Sear’s projectile path or stand behind a minion to avoid its stun.

Ekko.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand Ekko’s main damage. If Ekko catches you once and makes it hard to fight from the flank, get Zhonya’s Hourglass early.
Ekko.combo: Hit the target with Lillia E Swirlseed to slow them first, then hit the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! and finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. Use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby after applying Dream Dust with Lillia’s abilities, when an ally can wait for the sleep to take effect. This combo works well after Ekko E Phase Dive is down and you’ve dodged the area of Ekko W Parallel Convergence.
Ekko.escape: Don’t go deep when only Ekko E Phase Dive is down, since Ekko can escape with R Chronobreak. Look for a window when both Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko R Chronobreak are down. Then slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed and close the gap with Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!.
Ekko.fight: Before a fight, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build movement speed stacks. Avoid the area of Ekko W Parallel Convergence, slow him with Lillia E Swirlseed, then aim for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! while his movement is slowed. If Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, don’t chase deep just because he’s low on health.
Ekko.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly in succession instead of trying to get kills with solo ganks. Clip the edge of Lillia Q Blooming Blows through a group of monsters and hit the large monster with the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!. When ganking, wait for the opponent to move deeper into the lane, then roll Lillia E Swirlseed along the wall.
Ekko.phase: Early on, Lillia excels at clearing the jungle quickly and scaling rather than solo ganking, so don’t force kill fights with Ekko. Lillia gets stronger in the mid and late game as her damage over time and movement speed improve; look for a fight when Ekko R Chronobreak is down.
Ekko.teamfight: Instead of aiming for the center of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep! from the front, apply Dream Dust to multiple enemies with Lillia Q Blooming Blows from the flank. If Ekko engages on your allied damage dealers, use the slow from Lillia E Swirlseed to create distance, and avoid the marked area of Ekko W Parallel Convergence. If Lillia R Lilting Lullaby puts multiple enemies to sleep, coordinate with your allies to focus and wake them one at a time.
Ekko.watch: When you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, stay out of the marked area to avoid the stun and shield. Watch which direction Ekko Q Timewinder travels, and step out of its return path too. If you see the afterimage from Ekko R Chronobreak, don’t chase recklessly even if he’s low on health.

JarvanIV.build: Early on, buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots.
JarvanIV.combo: Slow them first with Lillia E Swirlseed, land the center hit of Lillia W Watch Out! Eep!, then finish with Lillia Q Blooming Blows. To use Lillia R Lilting Lullaby, first hit them with a skill to apply Dream Dust, then cast it when your allies can wait for the sleep to take effect.
JarvanIV.escape: Close the gap with Watch Out! Eep!.
JarvanIV.laning: Early on, clear camps quickly instead of trying to get kills with solo ganks. When ganking, wait until the enemy moves inside the lane, then roll Lillia E Swirlseed along a wall. Before engaging, hit a camp or minion with Lillia Q Blooming Blows to build up movement speed stacks.
